extracted.intended_audience: Scholarly peer reviewers for the American Journal of Political Science (AJPS)
extracted.subtask_short: AJPS peer review for journal articles
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for scholars reviewing manuscripts submitted to the American Journal of Political Science, outlining substantive evaluation criteria, recommendation categories, conflict-of-interest rules, and procedural expectations. Intended to guide reviewers on what to assess and how to frame their reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research question importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the manuscript addresses an interesting and important research problem or question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorizing and methodological quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the manuscript demonstrates high quality theorizing and/or state-of-the-art methodological use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of creativity or innovation of the research informing the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with relevant literature and contribution to knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the manuscript engages the relevant research literature and substantially contributes to the accumulation of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of communication to a general political science audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which the manuscript effectively and informatively communicates its contribution to a sophisticated general political science audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation — Must publish as is
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the manuscript requires no changes for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation — Must publish with minor revisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation should include a brief description of a small number of particular “doable” revisions stated in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation — Revise and resubmit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation must include a statement of specific improvements that would be required for publication, and should be made only when the research and manuscript fundamentals are sound (e.g., the theory, models, and hypotheses are strong, the dataset is complete, and the literature is consulted) and when successful revisions have the potential to produce a paper that makes a contribution suitable for the AJPS. It should be made only when the required revisions are viewed as highly likely to be successful with a reasonable amount of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation — Decline to publish
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation should be supported by reference to basic limitations in the theory, argument, research design, data and empirical analysis (where appropriate). It might reflect the belief that even substantial revisions could fail to address these concerns, or that even with successful revisions, the paper would not make the type of contribution expected for AJPS. Specific criticisms, provided in a constructive manner, are especially important in these reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews are advisory to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are advisory to the editorial team; final decisions reflect the entire review panel’s recommendations as well as the editors’ own evaluation of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be submitted as an anonymous file or inserted into a text box through Editorial Manager preferably no later than 30 days from receipt of the review request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit anonymously (file or text box) and aim to meet the 30-day timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest rules for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual should not review if they were an author’s doctoral dissertation supervisor, have been a co-author of an author in the past 5 years (with limited exceptions), are a colleague in an author’s department or comparable academic unit, or have a family or other personal relationship with an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential reviewers who have coauthored with one of the manuscript authors within the past five years are considered to have a Conflict of Interest and are not eligible to review, unless the coauthorship did not create a close professional relationship (e.g., large coauthor team where reviewer and author were not lead scholars and had little/no direct communication). Even if coauthorship did not create a close relationship, other factors (e.g., dissertation advisor) may create a COI. Individuals who have reviewed the manuscript for another journal are not automatically disqualified. The guidance leaves some discretion to manuscript authors to determine when coauthorship did not create a close professional relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend alternate reviewers when unable
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unable to review, please recommend 1-3 other qualified reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional tone and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to maintain a civil, professional tone in their reviews and to avoid sexist, racist, or otherwise offensive language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with the principles expressed in the APSA Guide to Professional Ethics in Political Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may use AI as part of their normal workflow (e.g., finding related papers, copyediting), but reviewers cannot use AI to directly evaluate a paper or write any part of a reviewer report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should also comply with Wiley’s AI guidelines for researchers and the full MPSA/AJPS AI policy linked by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical and flexible review length
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may be as long as the reviewer chooses; a 1–1.5 page length is typical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and specific criticisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific criticisms in a constructive manner, especially when recommending decline or major revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific, actionable criticisms help editors and authors understand the problems and possible remedies.
